alt_text: Slide 1 of 6. Your introduction does not have to begin with what went wrong.
Slide 2 of 6. Meeting someone new can feel like deciding how much history to bring into the room.
Slide 3 of 6. You can start with an interest, your work, a question, or what brought you there.
Slide 4 of 6. Share more as trust and relevance develop. Privacy is not dishonesty when the information is not theirs to require.
Slide 5 of 6. When a fact affects a shared decision, be truthful. A short introduction and a serious commitment need different levels of disclosure.
Slide 6 of 6. Share this with someone learning to meet people without presenting their whole history first.
